elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: "shall own all deliverables and work product prepared for Client under the Support Services"

elements.element: Vendor assigns such deliverables/work product to Customer

elements.evidence: "TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface"; insertion is "Subject to the license granted in Section 8(d)" and does not disturb 2(d)

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: "TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use such TrueLink Intellectual Property as part of those deliverables"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "Client retains all right, title and interest in and to Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, and all borrower, loan and other data submitted by or on behalf of Client or its customers"
"Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to TrueLink, or creates any joint ownership of, any of the foregoing"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: Only "TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface"; no express generic tools/know-how ownership

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for Customer's business
elements.evidence: licence is limited to "use such TrueLink Intellectual Property as part of those deliverables" — no worldwide, modification or sublicensing rights

reasons: The single inserted subsection (e) completes every preferred atomic element: Customer ownership of deliverables and work product with an express Vendor assignment, retention of Customer Content/IP/borrower-loan data, an anti-joint-ownership statement, and a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded Vendor IP.

Vendor's pre-existing IP retention is preserved by the untouched Section 2(d) Interface ownership sentence, and the insertion is expressly subject to the existing Section 8(d) licence, so no contradiction or dangling mechanic arises.

Fallback is not satisfied (no worldwide, modify or sublicense rights, no generic tools/know-how ownership statement), which is correct discipline: preferred-level drafting should not import fallback-only rights.
Minimality holds — one concise insert_after addressing an absent ownership clause, no rewrite of existing paragraphs and no broad new exceptions.
